title: donut block props
description: A whole in 2 to 6 parts (fewer reads better), as a ring whose centre says the highlighted part. Hover, a tap or the arrow keys lend the centre to another part.
x-ai-instructions: One chart says one thing: write takeaway as the finding, set highlight to the item that proves it, keep labels short (they are translated). On a narrated screen, give items an at anchor to the word that names them (see skill elabora-charts). Parts should add up to a whole; more than 5 parts reads badly: use bars.

takeaway.description: The sentence the chart proves, shown as its title: "Most incidents start with an email", not "Incidents by origin".

context.description: Only what neither the title nor the chart says (the unit, the population or the period the axes do not give), in one line under the title. Most charts need none; never a rephrasing of the takeaway.

source.description: Where the data comes from, shown under the chart.

parts.description: The parts, clockwise from the top.

id.description: Stable id of the item: highlights, voice beats and translations name it.

at.description: Narrated screens: the moment the voice brings this item ({ "line": "l2", "word": "phishing" }). It appears then, and the other items step back while the voice talks about it, until the next item's moment.

highlight.description: Id of the part that carries the idea: it takes the accent colour, the others step back.

unit.description: Unit written after the values (min, kg, €). "%" writes percentages as the language does (62 %, 62%).

center.description: What the centre of the ring says at rest.

totalLabel.description: Under the total, when center is total ("emails tested").

spotlightEnd.description: Narrated screens: when the voice is done with the items, so they all stand again and the highlight takes the colour. Default: the end of the line where the last item came.

revealOnBeats.description: Narrated screens with item moments: each item appears at its moment (true), or every item is there from the start and the moments only move the spotlight (false).
